label: sec:info-theory-intro
html:
The categorical framework of the QOU determines the information-theoretic structure of the universe. This chapter derives the Planck scale, the speed of light, mass--energy equivalence, the gravitational constant, and the operational entropy from the substrate parameter q and the Reeb derivation. We then develop the computational consequences: a categorical criterion for P \neq NP, a Turing-complete Skein machine, and a conformal cyclic cosmology where aeon boundaries are categorical horizons.

Emergent gravity arises from the information geometry of the Frobenius--Hopf state space. The Planck time equals one Reeb operation. The speed of light c_q = 1/(q-1) and the reduced Planck constant \hbar_q = (q-1)/q follow strictly from the substrate parameter.

The computational and cosmological implications include the P-bandwidth bound, statistical mechanics on the brane tower, and the horizon functor that implements Penrose's conformal cyclic cosmology within the QOU framework.
